question: Is residual species-by-route-night dependence confined to nearby stop pairs, or does it persist across the full spatial extent of routes?
population_and_prediction: Exactly the 2,835 weather-eligible strictly-prior-history pairs and fixed q matrices from the 72-h rainfall common-environment null.

geometry.coordinates: Pinned NAAMP physical SiteID coordinate file already used by the audited ERA5 antecedent-rain analysis.
geometry.pair_distance: Great-circle distance between every unordered pair of the ten physical SiteIDs in the focal wet route.
geometry.binning: Compute distance quartile boundaries from geometry only, before joining residual outcomes; then assign all species x route-night stop pairs to Q1-Q4 using those fixed boundaries.

statistic: Within each distance quartile, compute the same standardized residual-dependence D: sum e_j e_k divided by sum sqrt[q_j(1-q_j)q_k(1-q_k)].

null.generator: Independent Bernoulli draws from the same fixed heterogeneous q matrices.

outputs: distance quartile boundaries and median distance per quartile
observed D, null 95% interval and plus-one P for Q1-Q4
farthest-quartile D / nearest-quartile D ratio when estimable

interpretation.broad_spatial_dependence: Farthest distance quartile has D above its independent-null upper 95% bound with plus-one P < 0.05.
interpretation.boundary: Persistence at long distance argues against a dependence pattern confined to immediately neighbouring stops, but does not exclude shared hydrology, broad environmental forcing, cascading acoustic/social effects, or other latent route-night processes.

provenance: No distance binning, q model, seed, statistic, null, tail or interpretation rule may change after profile readback.
